/MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Issued at 114 AM MDT Sat Oct 24 2026

The work week will begin unsettled as a weak, inverted lee trough 
will be located to our south and east over the Central High Plains. 
This feature is associated with a rather broad mid-level shortwave 
trough, placing much of the Nebraska Panhandle at the inflection 
point between a weak downstream ridge located over the Upper 
Midwest, resulting in upper-level ageostrophic divergence and the 
formation of a weak surface low to our east. The strongest forcing 
for ascent at this time looks to set up over the Nebraska Panhandle 
and points further east, bringing chances for precipitation 
primarily east of the I-25 corridor during the day on Monday. 
Ensembles at this time have trended down from previous runs, with 
ECMWF ensemble means having 0.15-0.2" of QPF for Cheyenne, with 
locations in the Panhandle seeing upwards of 0.5", which would 
certainly help out with our drought conditions. Ensemble guidance 
suggests PWAT at or above the 95th percentile relative to 
climatology (~0.7") in the Panhandle, so heavy rain will be a threat 
especially if we see any convective elements over the area despite 
the main instability axis progged to remain well to the south and 
east over Kansas and Central Nebraska.

In terms of precipitation type, temperatures at this time look to be 
too warm for any snow (generally below 8000-9000 feet), as LREF 
guidance keeps 25th percentile minimum temperatures mainly in the 
mid to upper 30s east of the I-25 corridor, with low to mid-30s 
Monday morning for locations west of the Laramie Range. Places like 
Rawlins and Laramie will be away from the bulk of the forcing for 
ascent at this time, so will likely stay dry despite seeing slightly 
cooler temperatures. A weak cold front is progged to move through SE 
Wyoming and the NE Panhandle sometime late Monday into early 
Tuesday, which will result in slightly cooler overnight lows Tuesday 
morning, with locations west of I-25 waking up to temperatures at or 
slightly below freezing, and mid to upper 30s to the east. The 
shortwave trough ejects off to the north and east during the day 
Tuesday, placing us under a SW flow regime on the southern periphery 
of a rather amplified negatively-tilted shortwave trough lifting 
over Idaho and the Northern Great Basin. The strongest forcing for 
ascent looks to remain well to our north over Northern Wyoming and 
the Dakotas, so conditions for us look to remain mostly dry, with 
the exception of the Snowy and Sierra Madre Ranges which may manage 
to pick up some light snowfall, though ensemble guidance keeps 
totals under 1-2" and confined to the higher peaks. High 
temperatures on Tuesday are expected to be at or slightly above 
climatology with highs in the low 60s east of the Laramie Range, and 
low 50s to the west.

Wednesday, anticyclonic wave breaking over Northern British Columbia 
will serve to strengthen the geopotential height gradient associated 
with a closed low located off the coast of the Pacific Northwest. 
This, combined with an additional secondary shortwave trough located 
off the Oregon coast will serve to increase southwesterly 700-500 mb 
flow up to 50-60 knots, introducing the possibility for a high wind 
event, primarily for our wind-prone areas of Arlington and Bordeaux 
(tis' the season!). Model cross-sections along the I-80 corridor 
show mountain wave signatures that are reflective in the omega 
fields, however a mountain-top stable layer is lacking, which may be 
a limiting factor for a more high-end and widespread high wind 
event. As it stands, in-house random forecast guidance has around 
40% probabilities of Arlington experiencing high wind conditions 
Wednesday morning, with Bordeaux at around 20%, so while it may be 
gusty, stay tuned for potential high wind highlights as we get 
closer to this timeframe. Given gusty, downsloping conditions, high 
temperatures on Wednesday will continue to remain mild, with highs 
slightly above climatology in the low 60s east of the I-25 corridor, 
and 50s to the west. 

Heading towards the end of the work week, a negtaively-tilted ridge 
will begin to amplify, with the ridge axis located mainly to the 
east of our area, placing us under southwesterly flow. As 500 mb 
height anomalies increase to +1-2 sigma relative to climatology, can 
expect dry conditions and a slight warming trend.
